name: bold-1026-211845
hypothesis: Premise: fixed engine, judged stories. The small model misplays the champion's quarter-end judgement in repeatable ways, so take that judgement away: every quarter-end follows one stateless recipe that cannot pause growth for long, and all judgement goes into story choices, which move the statistics far more (lessons G5: v1 gained +44 Skill, +20 Network, +18 Output from stories against about +0, +4, +2 from Energy). Evidence from the champion's six digests. (1) Its risk state only ratchets up: the player never stepped down. scre-00003 took Lay low and reduce risk in 11 of 16 quarters, 10 in a row, including quarters that followed three calm HR remarks in a row, and refused new commitments in stories. At L3 its Skill and Network sat at their stall values (about 41 and 21) while Output, the only input still below its best, crept up about one point a quarter; it spent 18 months at L3 and finished at L4. ladd-00003 closed with 7 Lay-low quarters in a row and also finished at L4. The two L5 finishers took 6 and 2. (2) It reads 'weakest' as the smallest number. Before the first review ladd-00001 put two Energy points and the main action into Network while Network sat at its entry-level stall and Output was short; it was never promoted and was dismissed at month 24. (3) Its story rule pushes toward formal reports and escalations that cost the inputs a review reads: an anonymous HR report on a colleague and an open escalation over another team each cost two Network (ladd-00001, scre-00004), a formal written submission and a full incident response each cost Output, and ladd-00001 ended with Network at 0. Matteo's promotion study agrees: reviews are applied at the start of the review month, before its events and quarter-end, and at review time 11 of 15 unpromoted Haiku careers had dropped below their best on Network, Output or Skill, mostly through stories in the months just before the review. (4) The only careers past L5 (4 of 400 energy bots, Q 67-76) used a fixed quarter recipe with Apply for a key project every quarter and a Health point every quarter, and were promoted at each of their first three reviews. The recipe keeps G1 (Defuse after any risk wording, all career), G2 (a Health point most quarters, two when Health is low), G3 (Report results after a weak review, no Lay low), G4 (Output-first top-up) and G5 (honest ownership screens every story). What changes: risk is answered quarter by quarter, Lay low happens only at low Health or in the single quarter after strong risk wording, and the main action otherwise returns to Apply for a key project, the only published main action that raises Output, Skill and Network together. Why it should beat the champion: removing ratcheted Lay-low stretches keeps Output rising at L3 and L4, so completed careers reach L5 more often and earlier, lifting the level and wealth dimensions (46 and 34 for the champion, the two largest gaps). The story screens cut the pre-review losses of Network and Output that block first promotions, and promotion by the second review decides completion (12/14 completed when the first promotion came at the first review, 7/11 at the second, 0/13 later).
change: Replace the champion's single reactive Skill and its ratcheting Clear/Raised/Escalating state with three short Skills: a stateless quarter-end recipe (Health point, Defuse after any risk wording since the previous quarter-end, Output top-up, main action Apply for a key project unless Health is low, a weak review calls for Report results, or strong risk wording calls for one quarter of Lay low) and a story screen (honest ownership, then the Network cost of going against colleagues, then the Output cost of setting your own work aside, then Health and money).
predicted_behaviour: Notes at quarter-ends cite only feedback since the previous quarter-end and carry no Clear/Raised/Escalating label; about half of them say 'review next'. Main action: Apply for a key project in at least half of all quarters, Report results to your manager in the quarters after a C or D, Lay low and reduce risk in under a third of the champion's count and never for several quarters in a row while HR remarks are calm. Energy: Defuse legacy risk in every quarter whose preceding months carried risk wording, Health recovery in most quarters, Prepare report materials with the rest; no Skill learning or High-intensity work. Story notes name the Network or Output cost an option carries. Outcomes on race Haiku: completion at least the champion's (13 of 17), first promotion by the second review in most games, more than half of completed games at L5 or higher, completed level dimension above 46 and wealth above 34, risk control near the champion's 69.
refutation: Refuted if, with the same actor and environment, completion falls below the champion's, if trust-crisis exits or blow-ups per game rise (risk control of completed games clearly below 69), or if completed games do not end with higher level and wealth dimensions than 46 and 34. Manipulation check: if notes show a risk state kept across calm quarters, Lay low at comfortable Health after calm remarks, Skill learning or High-intensity work, or Apply for a key project in fewer than half of the quarters, the text was not followed and the result says nothing about the premise.
notes: fast race bold designer; premise: fixed engine, judged stories. A stateless quarter-end recipe modelled on the only careers that passed L5 (key project every quarter, Health point, Defuse on any risk wording), and all judgement moved into a short story screen. Brief premise 4 (separate quarter-end and story Skills), with guardrails G1-G5 kept. 632 words by wc -w including front matter (champion 393).
